title: Bounded clock simulation
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be an alphabet, let $e:\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ be an embedding, and let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $k$ work tapes, state set $S$, and stopping predicate $P:S\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. Fix an input $x$, a configuration $c$ whose state is $q$, a Boolean word $w$, a tape content $ct:\mathbb Z\to\mathrm{Option}(\Gamma)$, and a position $cp\in\mathbb Z$. Suppose that for every integer $p$ with $-1\le p\le |w|$, the content of this tape at $cp+p$ equals the content prescribed there by the word $w$ encoded using $e$. For every natural number $\tau$ no greater than the base-two value $\operatorname{Nat.ofDigits}(2, w.map(\mathrm{Bool.toNat}))$, if $M$'s configuration after $\tau$ steps is stopped (its state is absent or satisfies $P$), and every configuration at an earlier time is not stopped, then the machine obtained by adjoining a counter tape and using it to clock the simulation reaches, at some time $T\le 5\tau+2|w|+2$, a configuration whose simulated machine configuration is exactly $M$'s configuration after $\tau$ steps, whose state is the finish state carrying that configuration's state, and whose counter tape is patched with the encoding under $e$ of some Boolean word $w'$ of length $|w|$. At every time $u<T$ its state is neither a finish state nor a timeout state; at every time $u\le T$ its original work tapes, input-head position, and output agree with those of $M$ after some number $v\le\tau$ of steps, and its counter-head position lies between $cp-1$ and $cp+|w|$, inclusive.
